gap: No result ChatGPT got sets a screen's power draw against the minimum a laptop's port must supply (Intel: 15 W for a Thunderbolt 4 or 5 port, 7.5 W for a USB4 port). I could compute that headroom for one candidate only (Duex Max DS: 4.5 W, which is 60% of the USB4 minimum), and for none of the FOPO dual screens.
standout_why: I opened The Office Journal's USB-C extenders page, the iTechGuides 2025 guide, TechRadar's KYY X90E review (the one ChatGPT cited) and our own cited page, dealectric.com/best-laptop-screen-extender. The Office Journal and iTechGuides only say to 'verify your laptop's USB-C wattage' and give no figure for any screen or any port. TechRadar says one cable carries video and power and that a 15 W adapter comes in the box, but the part of the review I could see has no draw figure. Our own page already gives a draw for the Duex Max DS (4.5 W) and the Duex Float 2 Pro (7.5 W), but it never compares either one with a port's minimum. So the only new part is the port-minimum comparison, and it covers just one product.
decides: This confirms the one-screen segment and leaves the two-screen pick open. The Duex Max DS draws 4.5 W, inside the 7.5 W any USB4 port must supply and the 15 W a Thunderbolt 4 or 5 port must supply, so a true single cable is believable on those ports. I found no wattage for any FOPO dual screen (S1, S7, S10, S11), so this angle can't show that a FOPO screen runs on one cable without a second power lead. It can't place a FOPO product in the top three on power grounds. Angle A (video path and driver) has to decide whether FOPO places.

findings.label: Minimum power a laptop port must supply to accessories
findings.note: Row 'Minimum PC port power for accessories' in Intel's comparison table. These are spec minimums. A plain USB-C port that is neither USB4 nor Thunderbolt is not covered by this table.

findings.note: 4.5 W ÷ 7.5 W = 0.60; 4.5 W ÷ 15 W = 0.30. The 4.5 W draw comes from the Dealectric row above.
